Senses.Explanation: Literally, 'host within guest.' In the later systematic account of Linji's four guest-host configurations, this is the configuration named when 'the student has nostrils' (學人有鼻孔, 'the student has nostrils'). Records then raise the label as a public question and preserve different answers, including 'facing him, there is no companion.' This is one member of the fourfold set alongside host-within-host, guest-within-host, and guest-within-guest. The texts explicitly say that Linji's guest-host system differs from Caodong's, so the shared graphs must not blur the two school-specific things.
Senses.Note: Primary sense because the wave groups the term with Linji's four guest-host configurations. Family check with the four guest-host configurations (四賓主) and guest and host (賓主) preserves its explicit nostrils-definition and the stated contrast with Caodong. Split is required under §5 #0f.8: the corpus says the identically written category belongs to two different named systems.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如何是賓中主。穴云。入市雙瞳瞽。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Eye of Humans and Gods preserves a direct guest-within-host question with the answer 'entering the market, both pupils blind.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰如何是賓中主。師曰。對面無儔侶。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A public interview asks for host-within-guest; the master answers, 'facing him, there is no companion.'

Senses.Explanation: In Caodong guest-host discourse the same words name a position paired with host-within-guest's converse and with the bent-and-upright vocabulary. The Eye of Humans and Gods explicitly glosses Caodong's host-within-guest as 'function within essence' (用中體) and says this fourfold guest-host system is not the same as Linji's. In the Dongshan encounter, Dongshan asks 'what is host within guest?' and receives 'white clouds cover the green mountain'; another transmitted version assigns 'long years not leaving the house.' Later verse can say 'host within guest is precisely guest within host' and tell the hearer not to recognize a fixed pattern in reversal and accord. These are recorded formulas and answers, not an invitation to supply an interpretation beyond them.
Senses.Note: Separate school-specific referent, not a competing reading of one saying. Variant answers are retained as deployments within the Caodong positional category and are not split further.

Occurrences.Kwic: 洞山便問：「如何是賓中主？」云：「白雲蓋青山。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dongshan asks the positional question and receives 'white clouds cover the green mountain.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 如何是賓中主。師曰。長年不出戶。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A transmitted encounter gives the answer 'long years not leaving the house.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 賓中主即主中賓，逆順縱橫莫認真
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A verse pairs the two reciprocal position names and warns against fixing on their reversal and accord.

Occurrences.Kwic: 四賓主。不同臨濟。主中賓。體中用也。賓中主。用中體也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Eye of Humans and Gods explicitly says that this four-guest-host set differs from Linji's and glosses the Caodong host-within-guest position as function within essence.

AlternateTargets: the guest and the host in an encounter
Senses.Explanation: The paired roles of guest and host in a face-to-face meeting. The stock verdict 'guest and host stand out distinctly' (賓主歷然) states that the roles are distinct. Fixed forms carry the same pair across the records: Linji's 'guest-host phrase' (賓主句), 'one shout distinguishes guest and host' (一喝分賓主), and Zhaozhou's 'no-guest-no-host story' (無賓主話). Caodong records deploy the pair positionally in 'guest and host exchange places' (賓主互換), pair it with bent and upright (偏正), and expand it into host-within-guest, guest-within-host, host-within-host, and guest-within-guest. Linji's named 'four guest-and-host' (四賓主) is a taxonomy built from this same pair; the added graph 'four' names that lexical object, which has its own entry. It does not give the base pair a second referent.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide sense. Interchange, distinction, negation, positional compounds, and the fourfold taxonomy are deployments or larger compounds of the same guest-host pair. Linji and Caodong organize related labels differently, but the term 'guest and host' (賓主) itself continues to name the pair.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問師：「還有賓主也無？」師云：「賓主歷然。」師云：「大眾要會臨濟賓主句，問取堂中二首座。」便下座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linji says guest and host are perfectly distinct and names his guest-host phrase.

Occurrences.Kwic: 入，兩堂齊喝，賓主歷然。照用同時，本無前後，菱花對像，虛谷傳聲。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Linji Record places 'guest and host stand out distinctly' after two halls shout together.

Occurrences.Kwic: 洞山便問：「如何是賓中主？」云：「白雲蓋青山。」「如何是主中主？」云：「長年不出戶。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dongshan asks the host-within-guest and host-within-host questions, anchoring positional compounds built from the pair.

Occurrences.Kwic: 賓主互換，偏正不拘，至位融和，所謂無礙。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Caodong formula says guest and host exchange places while bent and upright are not fixed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 未免賓主相待，彼此回互。直須賓不是賓、賓中有主，主不是主、主中有賓，賓主交參、互換無位
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Guest and host are set against each other and mutually turn through each other before the positional compounds are named.

Occurrences.Kwic: 「如何是主看賓？」師云：「不待形言語。」問：「如何是主看主？」師云：「兩眼對兩眼。」問：「如何是賓看賓？」師云：「二俱是瞎漢。」師復云：「離卻四賓主，諸人道將一句來看。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A Linji-house catechism names the four guest-and-host taxonomy, a larger compound formed from the same paired roles.

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉臨濟大師四賓主賓看主
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A heading raises Master Linji's four guest-and-host and begins with guest examining host.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂，謂眾曰：我向行脚到南方火爐頭，有箇無賓主話，直至如今無人舉著。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Zhaozhou tells the assembly that he raised a no-guest-no-host story by a southern hearth and that nobody has yet addressed it.

Senses.PreferredTarget: the Han hound chases the clod
AlternateTargets: a Han hound pursuing a dirt clod
the Han-family hound runs after the clod
Senses.Explanation: Literally, "the Han hound chases the clod." The phrase occurs 64 times in 46 allowlisted texts. A Blue Cliff Record comment gives the named allusion: the hound of the Han family was a swift dog, capable of tracking the cunning hare of Zhongshan; the monk in Dongshan's cold-and-heat exchange is compared to that hound running up the steps after a reflected moon and finding no moon there. Across the corpus the compact phrase is repeatedly contrasted with "the lion bites the person" (師子咬人，韓獹逐塊): one address says, "you must have the lion bite the person; do not imitate the Han hound chasing the clod" (直須師子咬人，莫學韓獹逐塊). It also occurs as a verdict after answers in public exchanges and as a verse line on Zhaozhou's attendant case. Zen bends the old hunting-dog allusion into a stock contrast between the person and the thrown clod, but the entry goes no farther than the corpus's own lion/person and hound/clod pairing.
Senses.Note: The graph translated as "hound" (獹) names the famed dog in the corpus's own allusion, and the graph translated as "Han" (韓) identifies it as the hound of the Han family. One allusive sense covers the simile, verdict, verse, and contrast. The variant "lion bites the person" uses both bite graphs (咬 and 齩) in witnesses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 其僧一似韓獹逐塊。連忙上階。捉其月影相似。又問。如何是無寒暑處。山云。寒時寒殺闍黎。熱時熱殺闍黎。如韓獹逐塊走到階上。又却不見月影。韓獹乃出戰國策。云韓氏之獹駿狗也。中山之兔狡兔也。是其獹方能尋其兔。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The comment compares the monk to the hound pursuing a reflected moon, then explicitly identifies the hound allusion from the Strategies of the Warring States.

Occurrences.Kwic: 直須師子咬人，莫學韓獹逐塊。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The address directly commands: “you must have the lion bite the person; do not imitate the Han hound chasing the clod.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 頌云。飋飋風松。蕭蕭雨檜。師子咬人。韓獹逐塊。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A verse on Zhaozhou's attendant case ends with the fixed lion/person and hound/clod contrast.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧禮拜，師曰：師子齩人，韓獹逐塊。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: After the monk bows in a public exchange, the master gives the paired phrase as a verdict.
